## System Requirements

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/getting-started/configuration-requirements-for-user-registration>

User Registration & Membership System Requirements

# System Requirements
Outlines the minimum WordPress version, PHP requirements, and server specifications needed to run the User Registration & Membership plugin effectively.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

# System Requirements for User Registration & Membership

To use the User Registration & Membership plugin smoothly on your WordPress site, your server and WordPress setup must meet certain minimum requirements. These requirements help ensure the plugin runs reliably, securely, and with full functionality.

## Supported WordPress Version

The plugin requires your WordPress installation to be up-to-date:

✅ Your WordPress version should be 6.4 or higher.

🔎 Why this matters: Keeping WordPress updated improves security, compatibility, and performance. Many plugin features rely on the latest WordPress core functions.

### How to Check Your WordPress Version

Log in to your WordPress Dashboard

Scroll to the bottom of any admin page — the version number is shown in the footer

Or go to Dashboard → Updates to see your current version and update if needed

## PHP Version Requirements

PHP is the server-side language that powers WordPress. The plugin requires:

✅ PHP version 7.2 or higher.

⚠ Important: PHP versions older than 7.2 are not supported and may cause errors or lack feature support.

💡 PHP 7.2+ is recommended for:

Better speed and performance

Stronger security protections

Support for modern PHP features used by the plugin

## MySQL Database Version

Your WordPress database must use:

✅ MySQL 5.6 or higher.

💡 If your host uses MariaDB, which is a fork of MySQL, make sure it's the equivalent version (typically MariaDB 10.x and above).

## Recommended PHP Configuration Settings

To ensure the plugin works smoothly — especially for forms, uploads, and server tasks — these PHP settings should be configured properly:

**SettingRecommended ValueWhy it matterspost_max_size**
64M or more
Allows larger form submissions

**memory_limit**
256M or more
Lets complex scripts run reliably

**max_execution_time**
300 seconds
Prevents timeouts during processes

**upload_max_filesize**
64M or more
Supports file uploads in forms

💡 What these do: These settings control how much data your server can handle at once, especially when users upload files, when forms process data, or when PHP scripts run longer tasks.

## Required PHP Functions

Some features of the plugin rely on WordPress being able to make remote requests.

✔ WP Remote Get must be enabled on your server.

💡 If this is disabled, features like automatic updates, remote verification, or integrations may not work correctly.

## How to Check Your Server Requirements

Go to your WordPress Dashboard

Navigate to Tools → Site Health

Click the Info tab

Expand the Server section — you'll see your PHP version, database version, and other server details

👉 This page shows most of the required values (PHP version, max upload size, memory limit, etc.) so you can verify them quickly.

## How to Update PHP Version (cPanel)

If your server uses cPanel, you can often update PHP yourself:

Log in to cPanel (or ask your hosting support if you don't have access)

Find and click Select PHP Version or MultiPHP Manager under the Software section

Choose a PHP version 7.2 or higher

Click Save/Apply to update it

💡 Tip: After changing PHP, check your site front-end and admin area to make sure everything looks normal.

## Security Note

Using older PHP versions:

Exposes your site to security risks

May prevent the plugin from working correctly

Can lead to compatibility issues with other plugins and themes

Always aim to keep your PHP and WordPress core updated.

## Summary Checklist

WordPress: 6.4 or higher

PHP: 7.2 or higher

MySQL: 5.6 or higher

post_max_size: 64M

memory_limit: 256M

max_execution_time: 300 seconds

upload_max_filesize: 64M

WP Remote Get: enabled

## Final Tips

If you're not sure how to change server settings, contact your hosting provider support — they can help adjust PHP settings

Always backup your site before updating PHP or WordPress versions

After updating PHP or server configurations, revisit the Site Health page to confirm all settings are correct

## Install the User Registration & Membership Plugin (FREE)

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/getting-started/how-to-install>

Install User Registration & Membership Plugin

# Install the User Registration & Membership Plugin (FREE)
Step-by-step guide for installing the User Registration & Membership plugin via WordPress dashboard or manual upload methods.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

Would you like to add custom user registration to your WordPress site? User Registration & Membership allows you to create professional registration forms with a drag-and-drop builder, replacing WordPress's default registration system. This tutorial will show you how to install and activate the free version of the plugin.

Before installing the User Registration & Membership Plugin, ensure your WordPress environment meets the requirements listed in this doc.

## Installation Methods

There are two primary methods to install User Registration & Membership Plugin. Choose the method that best suits your comfort level and requirements.

## Method 1: Install from WordPress Admin Dashboard (Recommended)

This is the easiest and most common method for installing the plugin directly from the WordPress Plugin Repository.

### Step 1: Access Plugin Installation

Log in to your WordPress admin dashboard.

Navigate to Plugins > Add Plugin from the left sidebar.

You'll see the "Add Plugins" page with search functionality.

### Step 2: Search for the Plugin

In the search box (top right), type: User Registration & Membership.

Press Enter or click the search button.

Look for the plugin by WPEverest with the title "User Registration & Membership".

### Step 3: Install and Activate the Plugin

Click the Install Now button on the User Registration & Membership plugin card.

WordPress will download and install the plugin automatically.

Wait for the installation (usually 10-30 seconds) and click the Activate button that appears after installation.

Alternatively, go to Plugins > Installed Plugins and activate it from there.

Upon activation, you'll be redirected to the plugin's welcome screen.

## Method 2: Manual Upload Installation

Use this method if you've downloaded the plugin file separately or need to install a specific version.

### Step 1: Download the Plugin

Visit the WordPress Plugin Repository

Click the Download button to get the latest version

Save the .zip file to your computer (do not extract it)

### Step 2: Upload via WordPress Admin

In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add Plugin

Click the Upload Plugin button at the top of the page

Click Choose File and select the downloaded .zip file

Click Install Now to begin the upload process

### Step 3: Complete Installation

Wait for the upload and installation to complete

Click Activate Plugin to enable the functionality

You'll be taken to the plugin's initial setup screen

## Post-Installation Setup

After successful installation and activation, you must configure the plugin to meet your needs.

## Install and Activate User Registration and Membership (PRO)

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/getting-started/how-to-install-and-activate-premium-features>

Install User Registration & Membership Pro Plugin

# Install and Activate User Registration and Membership (PRO)
Pro Learn how to purchase, install, and activate User Registration & Membership Pro to unlock advanced features and premium add-ons for your WordPress site.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

Extend your website capabilities with WordPress add-ons. While the User Registration & Membership free version has essential registration and membership features, its premium version unlocks advanced tools. Here's how you can access the premium features and addons of the plugin:

## Step 1: Install User Registration & Membership Pro

To install WordPress addons for User Registration & Membership Premium on your site, you should buy its premium version. (If you've already installed the plugin, navigate to step 2.)

To purchase, visit wpuserregistration.com and choose any plans that suit you.

Next, log into your WPEverest account , and you'll see the dashboard.

Navigate to the Downloads tab and download the User Registration & Membership Pro (or the Free Version) file.

Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin in your WordPress dashboard.

Upload the .zip file, then Install and Activate the plugin.

You'll now see the setup dashboard; configure the plugin and complete the setup.

User Registration & Membership Pro works independently, no free version required!

## Step 2: Activating Your Premium License

### How to Activate User Registration Pro License?

After activating the plugin, you must enter the license key to use the premium features. Go to User Registration & Membership account on WPeverest > Dashboard > License Keys.

Copy your license key and come back to the WordPress dashboard.

You might get a notification to enter the license key; you can click on the notification and paste the license key. Otherwise, navigate to User Registration & Membership > Settings > License.

Under License Activation, paste the license key you copied from the WPEverest Account for User Registration & Membership. Click the Activate License button, and you're all set.

## Step 3: Unlocking Premium Features and Addons

Since the User Registration & Membership is an addon-based plugin, you will find various WordPress addons with unique features and functionality required for the registration and membership form.

Let's say you need advanced custom fields on your forms. You will then have to activate the User Registration -Advanced Fields addon.

Follow the guidelines below to install and activate the User Registration & Membership premium addons:

### Method 1: Direct Activation (Recommended)

You can directly install the addon from your WordPress dashboard if you have activated the plugin with a license key.

Ensure your license is active (User Registration & Membership > Settings > License).

Next, click on User Registration & Membership > Addons. Here, you can find all the available features and addons based on your plugin's pricing plan. You can also view the addon list by category, such as Membership, Ecommerce, Security, Integration, Design, and more.

Click on any tabs to explore the features. To Activate any modules, features, or addons that are included in your plan (e.g., Advanced Fields, WooCommerce Integration), you can toggle.

Now, you can use the premium features and addons on your website. To deactivate any addon, module, or feature, you can toggle back.

### Method 2: Manual Upload

You can also manually upload the addon file as you did for the plugin through your WPEverest Account Dashboard. To add the addon manually:

Log in to your WPeverest account and go to Downloads.

Download individual addon ZIP files.

Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin and upload the .zip file as we did for the plugin.

Once the plugin is installed, it will ask to activate; click the Activate Plugin button.

We have detailed documentation on how to use each module and addons; you can explore them as per your need.

## Troubleshooting Tips

License Not Activating? Double-check your key in your WPeverest account.

Can't activate addon? Ensure your plan includes the feature. Contact support if issues persist.

Conflict Errors? Temporarily deactivate other plugins to test compatibility.

## Re-run Setup Wizard

Re-run User Registration Setup Wizard in WordPress

# Re-run Setup Wizard
Re-run the Setup Wizard to reconfigure plugin settings, create required pages, and update your initial User Registration & Membership configuration.
Last updated on Aug 7, 2026

## Overview

The Setup Wizard helps you configure the basic settings of the **User Registration & Membership** plugin right after installation, such as creating the required pages and choosing your default settings. If you skipped the wizard the first time, closed it before finishing, or simply want to review and update your initial configuration, you can re-run it at any time. Once you complete the wizard again, your registration, login, and account pages will be set up correctly, and your plugin settings will be up to date.

## Access Path

User Registration & Membership → Tools → Setup Wizard

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Log in to your WordPress admin dashboard.

Go to **User Registration & Membership → Tools** from the left sidebar menu.

On the **Tools** page, you'll see three tabs: **Logs**, **System Info**, and **Setup Wizard**.

Click on the **Setup Wizard** tab.

You'll be redirected to the wizard. Follow the on-screen instructions to go through each setup step again.

Once you've completed every step, your settings will be saved and ready to use.

## Tools Page Overview

Tab
Description

Logs
Displays a record of plugin activity, useful for troubleshooting.

System Info
Shows details about your site's server and environment, often needed when contacting support.

Setup Wizard
Lets you re-run the initial onboarding process to reconfigure your plugin settings.

Re-running the Setup Wizard does not delete your existing forms or settings. It simply walks you through the same setup steps again so you can review or update your configuration.

## Closing Section

That's it! After completing the Setup Wizard again, your **User Registration & Membership** plugin will have all the essential pages and settings configured correctly. You can revisit the wizard anytime from **Tools → Setup Wizard** if you need to make further changes.

## Set up Wizard Walkthrough

<https://docs.wpuserregistration.com/getting-started/set-up-wizard-walkthrough>

User Registration Setup Wizard: Step-by-Step Guide

# Set up Wizard Walkthrough
A step-by-step guide to configuring the User Registration & Membership plugin through its initial setup wizard, covering paid, free, and basic registration options.
Last updated on Jul 14, 2026

The Setup Wizard guides you through the initial configuration of User Registration & Membership. This guide covers all three setup options and shows you exactly what to expect at each step.

## Before You Begin

Make sure you have:

User Registration & Membership plugin installed and activated

WordPress admin access

A clear idea of whether you need paid memberships, free memberships, or basic registration

## Step 1: Launch the Setup Wizard

When you first activate the plugin, you'll see a welcome message. Click the Get Started button to launch the Setup Wizard.

The wizard uses a 4-step progress indicator: Welcome → Membership → Payment → Finish

## Step 2: Choose Your Setup Type

You'll see three setup options. Choose the one that matches your needs:

### Option 1: Paid Membership Setup

Follow these steps if you selected Paid Membership.

Create Your First Membership Plan. You'll be prompted to create your first paid membership plan. Fill in:

Plan Name — e.g., 'Premium Member', 'Gold Plan'

Type — Select 'Free', 'One-Time Payment' or 'Subscription Based'

Price — Set the price (e.g., $29.99)

Billing Cycle (only for subscription plan): Choose the number for recurring day/week/month/year for your plan.

Access — Choose content to restrict

You can add more membership plans later. Click **Next **to continue.

2. Configure Payment Gateway. Choose your preferred currency and choose which payment methods to enable: PayPal, Stripe or Offline Payment method.

At minimum, enable one payment gateway. Click Next after configuration.`

Complete the setup by click on **Go to Dashboard**. **Registration Page, My Account Page, Login Page, **and **Membership Pricing Page **will be created for you after the setup.

### Option 2: Free Membership Setup

Follow these steps if you selected Free Membership.

Follow these steps if you selected Paid Membership.

Create Your First Membership Plan. You'll be prompted to create a free membership plan. Fill in:

Plan Name — e.g., 'Member A', 'Web Plan'

Type — Select 'Free' plan that's already selected for you.

Access — Choose content to restrict. Click on **+Content** and **Whole Site or Pages or Posts **and **select pages or posts.**

You can add more membership plans later. Click **Next **to continue.

Complete the setup by click on **Go to Dashboard**. **Registration Page, My Account Page, Login Page, **and **Membership Pricing Page **will be created for you after the setup.

## Option 3: Advanced Registration Setup

Follow these steps if you selected Advanced Registration.

1. Configure User Approval and Login. Click on the dropdown from **User Approval And Login Option**:

Auto Approval with Manual Login — Users are approved automatically but must log in manually

Auto Approval with Auto Login — Users are approved and logged in immediately

Admin Approval — You manually review each registration

Auto Approval After Email Confirmation — Users verify email before accessing the site

2. **Assign Default User Role**: Choose the WordPress role assigned to new users:

Subscriber (recommended) — Can only manage their profile

Contributor — Can write posts but not publish

Author — Can publish their own content

Editor — Can manage all content

Click Next to continue.

Complete the setup by click on **Go to Dashboard**. **Registration Page, My Account Page, Login Page, **and **Membership Pricing Page **will be created for you after the setup.

## What Happens After Setup

Regardless of which setup type you chose, after completing the wizard:

All required pages are created and published

A default registration form is available and ready to use

User approval and role settings are configured

You can start accepting registrations immediately

All settings can be modified later from the plugin dashboard

## Re-running the Setup Wizard

If you need to change your initial configuration or want to switch between setup types, you can re-run the wizard at any time:

Go to User Registration & Membership → Tools in your WordPress dashboard

Click the Setup Wizard tab

Follow the same steps outlined above for your chosen setup type

Re-running the wizard will not delete your existing forms, pages, or user data. It only updates the configuration options you change during the wizard process.
